name: mcom-seasonal
title: MCoM under seasonal light: a sustained, oscillating chemostat community
question:
When the same MCoM phytoplankton-heterotroph pair is placed in an open,
dilution-driven box (a chemostat) with a steady nutrient inflow but a
sinusoidally varying, annual light supply, does the community reach a
sustained regime that blooms and recedes with the seasons rather than washing
out or running to a fixed point?
hypothesis:
Under a constant dilution D = 0.1/day that continuously removes biomass and a
steady inflow of 10 mM inorganic nitrogen, an unforced community would settle
to a steady state. Adding an annual sinusoid to the irradiance (peak at
mid-year) should make phytoplankton growth -- and therefore the whole coupled
community -- rise and fall on a one-year cycle: the phytoplankton should bloom
under the summer light maximum and recede under the winter minimum, while the
dilution keeps the community from either washing out or over-accumulating.
objective:
Run the `mcom_seasonal` composite (the co-culture parameter set placed in a
D = 0.1 chemostat with N_ext = 10 mM steady inflow and irradiance
5 + sinus(6, 365)) for 1460 days (4 seasonal cycles) and verify (a) the
community is sustained -- phytoplankton never washes out in the established
regime -- and (b) the community draws the supplied nitrogen well down. The
seasonal oscillation itself is quantified (peak/trough ratio) and shown in the
time-series visualization.
description:
Wraps the `viva_mcom.composites.coculture.mcom_seasonal` generator -- the same
single-phytoplankton / single-heterotroph parameters as `mcom-coculture`, but
in an open box: dilution rate D = 0.1/day, a constant inflowing DIN
concentration N_ext = 10 mM entering through MCoM's D*(N_ext - N) exchange
term, and a seasonally varying irradiance `5 + sinus(6, 365, 182.5)` (annual
period, summer peak). This exercises MCoM's environmental-fluctuation grammar
(the `sinus` forcing) and its dilution/exchange transport term together.

Achieved (1460-day run, established regime = second half): the phytoplankton
settles into a sustained annual cycle swinging between ~0.42 and ~0.89
(1e6 cells/mL), a peak/trough ratio of ~2.1; the heterotroph tracks it,
oscillating around ~1.86; inorganic nitrogen is held near 2.1 mM (from a 10 mM
inflow), i.e. the community consumes ~80% of the supplied nitrogen. The
community neither washes out nor runs away -- the seasonal light sets the
rhythm, the dilution sets the ceiling.

expected_behavior.name: community-sustained-under-dilution
expected_behavior.en: The phytoplankton is sustained under continuous dilution: its minimum total density over the established (second-half) regime stays above 0.15, i.e. it never washes out.
expected_behavior.rationale: A dilution rate of 0.1/day continuously removes 10% of the standing biomass per day; a community that could not sustain growth against it would collapse toward zero. A second-half minimum above 0.15 shows the phytoplankton persists through even the winter light minimum. Achieved second-half minimum is 0.425; 0.15 sits well below that yet decisively above washout (~0).

expected_behavior.name: nutrient-drawn-down-in-chemostat
expected_behavior.en: The community draws the supplied nitrogen well down: mean inorganic nitrogen over the second half stays below 5.0 mM against a 10 mM inflow.
expected_behavior.rationale: The inflow sets DIN toward 10 mM; the standing concentration reflects the balance between supply and biological uptake. A second-half mean below 5.0 mM (i.e. more than half the inflow consumed) evidences an active, nutrient-limited community. Achieved second-half mean is 2.13 mM; 5.0 fails a community that barely draws nitrogen down (which would sit near the 10 mM inflow).

behavior_tests.name: community-sustained-under-dilution
behavior_tests.description:
Minimum total phytoplankton density over the second half of the run exceeds
0.15 (1e6 cells/mL) -- the community is not washed out by the 0.1/day dilution.

provenance.note: Dilution removes 10%/day; a non-sustaining community collapses toward 0. Achieved second-half minimum is 0.425. 0.15 sits decisively above washout and well below the achieved trough.

behavior_tests.name: nutrient-drawn-down-in-chemostat
behavior_tests.description:
Mean inorganic nitrogen over the second half is below 5.0 mM against a 10 mM
steady inflow -- the community consumes a large fraction of the supply.

provenance.note: Inflow N_ext = 10 mM; achieved second-half mean is 2.13 mM (~80% consumed). 5.0 fails a community that barely draws nitrogen down.

embed_visualizations.name: seasonal-succession
embed_visualizations.description: Phytoplankton and heterotroph vs inorganic nitrogen over 4 seasonal cycles -- a sustained community oscillating on the annual light cycle (~2.1x peak/trough) without washing out, with DIN held near 2.1 mM against a 10 mM inflow.

conclusion:
Both behaviour tests pass. Under 0.1/day dilution with a 10 mM nitrogen inflow
and annually-varying light, the community reaches a sustained regime: the
phytoplankton oscillates between 0.42 and 0.89 (2.1x peak/trough) on the
one-year light cycle without washing out, the heterotroph tracks it around
1.86, and inorganic nitrogen is held near 2.1 mM (~80% of the inflow consumed).
MCoM's seasonal-forcing (sinus) grammar and dilution transport reproduce a
stable, oscillating open-system community.
